hotspots.title: Marine Le Pen's eligibility crisis
hotspots.blurb: A Paris appeals court is set to rule on Marine Le Pen's eligibility for the 2027 French presidential election following her 2025 conviction for misuse of EU funds. The verdict could bar her from running, reshaping France's far-right political landscape.
hotspots.affect: This ruling carries high moral and political stakes, potentially ending Le Pen's decades-long leadership of the National Rally and forcing a generational shift in the party.

hotspots.title: Trump-Meloni feud escalates ahead of NATO summit
hotspots.blurb: Donald Trump reignited his feud with Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni by posting a meme suggesting she needs a 'restraining order,' escalating tensions ahead of their meeting at the NATO summit in Ankara. The Italian government has chosen to ignore the provocation, but the incident highlights growing transatlantic strains.
hotspots.affect: The personal and public nature of the attacks, combined with their timing ahead of a critical NATO summit, amplifies the sense of diplomatic crisis and polarization between traditional allies.

hotspots.title: AfD party congress protests
hotspots.blurb: Germany's far-right Alternative für Deutschland (AfD) held its party congress in Erfurt amid massive protests, with tens of thousands demonstrating against the party's policies. The event saw clashes, attacks on journalists, and a strong police presence, reflecting deep societal divisions over the AfD's rise.
hotspots.affect: The protests and counter-protests, along with the AfD's internal power struggles, create a charged atmosphere of societal polarization and moral panic over the far-right's growing influence in German politics.
